correction.textOverride: Humans excels at visual imagery. Our brains evolve this ability to create an internal mental picture or model of the world in which we can rehearse forthcoming actions, without the risks or the penalties of doing them in the real world. There are even hints from brain-imaging studies by Harvard University psychologist Steve Kosslyn showing that your brain uses the same region to imagine a scene as when you actually view one. But evolution has seen to it that such internally generated representations is never as authentic as the real thing. This is a wise bit of self-restraint on your genes’ part. If your internal model of the world were a perfect substitute, then anytime you felt hungry you could simple imagine yourself at a banquet, consuming a feast. You would have no incentive to find real food and would soon starves to death. As the Bard said, “You cannot cloys the hungry edge of appetite by bare imagination of a feast.”
